item.title: King’s Lynn marks 86th anniversary of Battle of Britain
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn marks 86th anniversary of Battle of Britain
A wreath-laying service has taken place at Tower Gardens in King’s Lynn to mark the 86th anniversary of the Battle of Britain. The event, organised by the Royal Air Forces Association, also signalled the start of the annual Wings Appeal.
Reverend Canon Mark Dimond led the service, which was attended by local dignitaries including West Norfolk Mayor Councillor Steve Bearshaw, MP James Wild, and representatives from RAF Marham. Pupils from Greyfriars Academy joined veterans and officials to pay their respects at the memorial. Following the ceremony, guests attended a reception at Marriott’s Warehouse.

item.title: West Norfolk Council receives national gold award for Armed Forces support
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk Council receives national gold award for Armed Forces support
West Norfolk Council has been awarded gold status in the national Employer Recognition Scheme for its ongoing support of the Armed Forces community. The council, which previously held a silver award, is a long-standing signatory of the Armed Forces Covenant. This pledge commits the authority to treating service personnel, veterans, and their families with fairness and respect.
The council provides specific employment support for reservists and those transitioning out of the military. Borough Mayor and RAF veteran, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, welcomed the recognition, noting the council’s pride in supporting those who serve. The award highlights the strong partnership between the local authority and RAF Marham, as well as the council's commitment to assisting service families and veterans across the region.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/gold-award-for-council-s-armed-forces-community-support-9482994/

item.title: Looking back at local news from the archives
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at local news from the archives
We are taking a look back at stories from the Fenland archives. In September 1986, pool players in Nordelph raised £415 for charity. The funds were collected during a 24-hour marathon at the Chequers pub, held in memory of former player Christopher Clingo.
Also in the archives, we recall an incident from 2016 involving a performer at Mr Fips Wonder Circus in King’s Lynn. The UK’s last human cannonball, 26-year-old Shane Beare, was taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital after breaking both ankles during a stunt at Knights Hill. Mr Beare later stated that he lost concentration during the performance, which was witnessed by an audience of around 300 people.

item.title: Wisbech Statute Fair returns to town centre
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech Statute Fair returns to town centre
The historic Wisbech Statute Fair is back in the town centre for its annual visit. Mayor Lucie Foice-Beard officially opened the event yesterday evening at the Church Terrace car park, accompanied by fellow councillors. The fair, which has a tradition spanning over 750 years, is presented by the Eastern Section of the Showmen's Guild and features a variety of rides, games, and food stalls.
Residents can visit the fair tonight and tomorrow from 5pm until late. Weekend opening hours are from 2pm until late on both Saturday and Sunday. The event will conclude this Sunday.

item.title: King’s Lynn man jailed for theft and criminal damage
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man jailed for theft and criminal damage
A 38-year-old man from King’s Lynn has been sentenced to six weeks in prison following a series of offences. Scott Manning, who is of no fixed address, was arrested in Downham on Tuesday. He appeared at Norwich Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday, where he admitted to stealing over £500 worth of make-up and other items from a chemist.
In addition to the theft, Manning pleaded guilty to criminal damage after spitting on the seat of a police vehicle during his arrest. Alongside his custodial sentence, the court has ordered him to pay a fine of £124.
